summary: Elevated time-to-first-token for short-chat payloads after runtime 2.3.1 + model repin
description:
Issue summary:
Elevated time-to-first-token (TTFB) observed for short chat prompts (<32 tokens) from LuminaApps on the Hosted API after the runtime 2.3.1 deploy and model repin performed 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC.

Impact:
- A subset of customer chat sessions see 1.0–3.5s additional delay to first token.
- Affects primarily small prompts and bursty traffic patterns; medium/long prompts show normal tail latency.
- Customer reports degraded UX for chat snippets used in search/autocomplete flows.

Environment:
- Hosted API (prod) in us-east-1, customer using dedicated pool with session-affinity.
- Runtime: 2.3.1 (rolled 2026-03-09), Model repin to redwood-2.0 (quantized variant) at same window.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send short chat completion request (system + single-turn user prompt ~8–16 tokens) via Hosted API with session affinity header.
2) Observe websocket/HTTP streaming start time and time-to-first-token metric.
3) Repeat at scale (50–200 qps) to reproduce bursty behavior.

Observed logs / metrics snippets:
- api-gw logs: upstream_connect_time spike correlated with 504s early, but most requests return 200 with delayed first-token.
- edge-proxy: TLS handshake durations stable; occasional renegotiation entries for connections with affinity to pool-a.
- serving-runtime: increased per-request setup time before KV cache warm path (~800ms per affected request).
- session-manager: affinity mapping shows 18% of user sessions sent to a new runtime shard (shard-7) after repin.

Temporary workaround attempted by Support:
- Forced customer traffic to a stable pool via temporary routing override (re-routed to pool-b). Observed immediate reduction in TTFB for affected sessions.
- Scoped rate-limit on pool-a to reduce burst pressure; partial improvement.

Notes: This is not a full outage and does not generate widespread 5xxs. Reproducible via short prompts + session affinity and burst pattern.
